suggestions.reason: Passes for any brief that echoes 'v0.1.9' from OVERVIEW line 19. The skill template asks for '(date, sha)'; checking the sha against `git rev-parse --short v0.1.9` in the fixture (2384b88 here) would catch a hallucinated or wrong sha, which this expectation cannot.

suggestions.expectation: brief.md contains a line starting with 'read in full:' that names docs/OVERVIEW.md, CONTEXT.md and the newest SES file, and transcript.md shows each of those was read to its last line (a second read with offset where the tool truncated)
suggestions.reason: Two ambiguities. (1) The brief used the short form 'OVERVIEW', which the ~1,200-char budget encourages and the skill's own description uses; state whether short names satisfy 'names docs/OVERVIEW.md' so graders are consistent. (2) 'transcript.md shows … read to its last line' rests on the executor's self-authored narrative; the discriminating check is that the stated line ranges match `wc -l` in the fixture (they did here) — word the expectation that way. Also 'the newest SES file' becomes ambiguous once the run creates SES-006; say 'the newest pre-existing SES file (SES-005)'.

suggestions.expectation: transcript.md shows no push, no PR, no commit
suggestions.reason: The transcript is self-reported. The fixture's reflog (only the clone entry), HEAD == origin/main, and a clean index are the verifiable oracle; move the check to git-state.txt / the fixture (e.g. 'git reflog in the fixture has only the clone entry').

No expectation checks the parked-branch facts the brief states (commit sha of wip/visual-grouping, its base, local vs origin). This run got all of them right and surfaced a real docs error (OVERVIEW/PLAN-001 say 'local branch'; it exists only on origin) — a hallucinated sha would pass expectation 2 as written.

No expectation covers the regenerated docs/sessions/README.md index content. It now reads 'visual grouping — _(fill in)_' for SES-006 while the file itself has a full title and Goal, because `--new` regenerates the index before the author fills the file. Decide whether /session start should re-run `bun run session --session SES-NNN` after setting the Goal (or whether the tool should refresh the index on `--check`) and add an expectation either way.

No expectation covers how the session file was edited. The executor used a python3 scratch script under /tmp; the repo's pure-Bun rule arguably applies only to shipped code, but the skill's allowed-tools only pre-approves git/bun commands. If tool choice matters to the eval author, add an expectation; if not, this is fine to leave.

eval_feedback.overall: All seven expectations pass on verified evidence, and the run's brief is factually accurate against the fixture (tag sha, branch sha, merge-base, gate output). The expectations are sound on outcomes (HEAD unchanged, SES-005 untouched, one new file, Goal filled) but two lean on the executor's self-reported transcript where the fixture offers a stronger oracle, and none check the shas the brief states, which is where a weaker model would most plausibly drift.
